overview.contentSubtitle: Learn the idea, then see it in action.

data-structure.title: Data Structure
data-structure.description: Build a strong foundation in the structures and algorithms that power modern software. Explore each concept through an interactive visualizer.

advanced-data-structure.title: Advanced Data Structure
advanced-data-structure.description: Study tree structures that organize hierarchical data and keep operations efficient as collections grow.

information-theory-compression.title: Information Theory & Data Compression
information-theory-compression.description: Explore how information is represented efficiently through lossless and lossy compression, with interactive algorithm visualizations.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.description: Understand indexed storage, access, updates, and common array operations.

stacks.title: Stacks
stacks.description: Explore last-in, first-out behavior with push, pop, and peek operations.

queues.title: Queues
queues.description: See how first-in, first-out structures manage data and scheduling.

linked-lists.title: Linked Lists
linked-lists.description: Follow node connections in singly, doubly, circular, and ordered lists.

sorting.title: Sorting Algorithms
sorting.description: Compare how sorting strategies order data, one operation at a time.

searching.title: Searching Algorithms
searching.description: Trace linear, binary, and jump search to find values efficiently.

graphs.title: Graphs
graphs.description: Model connected data and explore traversals and shortest paths.

trees.title: Binary Search Trees
trees.description: Insert, find, and remove values while exploring tree traversals.

avl-tree.title: AVL Tree
avl-tree.description: See how self-balancing rotations preserve logarithmic tree height.

red-black-tree.title: Red-Black Tree
red-black-tree.description: Explore node coloring, insertion fix-ups, and balanced search paths.

lossless-compression.title: Lossless Compression
lossless-compression.description: Compress data without losing information, then reconstruct the original input exactly.

lossy-compression.title: Lossy Compression
lossy-compression.description: Reduce data size by discarding information that may be less noticeable.

lossless.description: The decoded output is identical to the original input.
lossless.partsDescription: Choose a method group to see its algorithms and availability.
lossless.dictionaryDescription: Replace repeated sequences with references to symbols that have already appeared.
lossless.huffmanDescription: Represent frequent symbols with shorter prefix-free codewords.
lossless.arithmeticDescription: Represent a message as a narrowing interval, including floating-point and adaptive variants.
lossless.adaptiveHuffmanDescription: Update the Huffman tree as each symbol is read, without a precomputed frequency table.
lossless.modifiedHuffmanDescription: Group symbols at or below a probability threshold into Others and append their fixed-width source codes.
lossless.slideRule: Slide convention: matches cannot extend past the candidate suffix in the search buffer. If longest matches tie, choose the nearest occurrence.

lossy.description: Lossy predictive methods (DPCM and linear prediction) and transform coding with quantization and DCT are planned for a future lesson.

dictionary.lz77Description: Encode repeated sequences as a backward offset, a match length, and the next symbol.
dictionary.lz78Description: Build a dictionary of phrases while emitting each new phrase as an index and next symbol.
dictionary.lzwDescription: Encode dictionary phrases as integer codes while growing the shared phrase table.

visualizer.title: LZ77 interactive visualizer
visualizer.encodedInputHelp: Paste the encoded data from this algorithm or provide a valid JSON payload.
visualizer.emptyEncoded: Run compression to create encoded data.
visualizer.arithmeticModelHelp: The lecture example uses {"A":80,"B":2,"C":18}. Frequencies need not equal the message length.
visualizer.thresholdHelp: Symbols with probability less than or equal to this threshold use the Others code plus a fixed-width symbol code.
visualizer.windowHelp: Choose the number of symbols visible in each sliding window.
visualizer.decompressHelp: Compress the input first, then decode its tags step by step.
visualizer.emptyTokens: Run compression to produce LZ77 tags.
visualizer.emptyDecoded: Run decompression to rebuild the input.
visualizer.compressionNote: {{positionBits}} offset + {{lengthBits}} length + 8 next-symbol bits per tag.
visualizer.asciiOnly: The slide estimate assumes 8-bit input symbols.
visualizer.noSteps: Start compression or decompression to follow each algorithm step.
visualizer.slideNote: This follows the worked lecture example. The Python sample's cyclic matching can extend beyond the available search-buffer suffix, so that behavior is intentionally not used here.

steps.lz78Start: Start with {{length}} symbols and an empty phrase dictionary.
steps.lz78Hit: The phrase “{{phrase}}” is already entry {{index}}; keep extending it.
steps.lz78Miss: The phrase “{{phrase}}” is new. Emit its previous prefix index and next symbol.
steps.lz78Emit: Emit LZ78 tag {{tokenIndex}} and add phrase “{{phrase}}” as dictionary entry {{dictionaryEntry}}.
steps.lz78Terminal: The input ends on known phrase “{{phrase}}”; emit its terminal tag.
steps.lz78Complete: LZ78 compression is complete: {{tokenCount}} tag(s), {{dictionarySize}} phrase(s).
steps.lz78DecodeStart: Begin decoding {{tokenCount}} LZ78 tags with the empty phrase at index 0.
steps.lz78DecodeTag: Read tag {{tokenIndex}} and append phrase “{{phrase}}” to the output.
steps.lz78DecodeTerminal: Read the terminal tag {{tokenIndex}} and append phrase “{{phrase}}”.
steps.lzwStart: Initialize LZW with {{alphabetSize}} ASCII symbols; new phrase codes start at {{firstNewCode}}.
steps.lzwAdd: Emit code {{code}} for “{{phrase}}”; add “{{added}}” as code {{addedCode}}.
steps.lzwComplete: LZW compression is complete with {{codeCount}} code(s) and {{dictionarySize}} dictionary entries.
steps.lzwDecodeStart: Decode {{codeCount}} codes using the {{alphabetSize}}-symbol initial alphabet.
steps.lzwDecodeCode: Code {{code}} expands to “{{entry}}”; add “{{added}}” as dictionary code {{addedCode}}.
steps.lzwDecodeSpecial: The next code equals the next dictionary index; reconstruct “{{entry}}” from the previous phrase.
steps.huffmanStart: Count the frequency of each of the {{length}} input symbols.
steps.huffmanMerge: Merge the two lowest-frequency nodes ({{left}} and {{right}}) into a node of weight {{frequency}}.
steps.huffmanComplete: Huffman encoding is complete: {{symbolCount}} symbols in {{bitLength}} bit(s).
steps.modifiedHuffmanGroups: Group symbols with probability at most {{threshold}} into Others: {{others}} (frequency {{othersFrequency}}).
steps.huffmanDecodeStart: Decode {{bitLength}} bits using the supplied prefix-free codebook.
steps.huffmanDecode: Bits through position {{bitIndex}} form code {{code}} for “{{symbol}}”.
steps.adaptiveStart: Start with a single NYT (not-yet-transmitted) leaf for {{length}} input symbols. Assign {{shortWidth}}-bit short codes to alphabet {{alphabet}}.
steps.adaptiveNew: Symbol {{index}} (“{{symbol}}”) is new. Send the NYT path followed by short code {{shortCode}}, split the leaf, and update the tree.
steps.adaptiveKnown: Symbol {{index}} (“{{symbol}}”) is already in the model. Send its current path, then update the tree.
steps.adaptiveComplete: Adaptive Huffman encoding is complete with {{symbolCount}} symbols and {{eventCount}} events.
steps.adaptiveDecodeStart: Decode {{eventCount}} adaptive Huffman events from an initial NYT leaf.
steps.adaptiveDecode: Decode symbol {{index}} (“{{symbol}}”) from path {{code}} and update the model.
steps.arithmeticStart: Count {{length}} symbols and form cumulative intervals over a total frequency of {{total}}.
steps.arithmeticEncode: Symbol {{index}} (“{{symbol}}”) narrows the interval using cumulative range [{{cumulativeLow}}, {{cumulativeHigh}}) to [{{lowValue}}, {{highValue}}).
steps.arithmeticComplete: The message is represented by the rational code {{code.decimal}} inside [{{low.decimal}}, {{high.decimal}}).
steps.arithmeticDecodeStart: Decode {{length}} symbols from rational value {{code.decimal}} using total frequency {{total}}.
steps.arithmeticDecode: Value selects symbol {{index}} (“{{symbol}}”); narrow the interval to [{{lowValue}}, {{highValue}}).
steps.compressStart: Start with {{length}} input symbols. At each cursor, inspect the search and look-ahead buffers.
steps.window: At cursor {{cursor}}, compare the look-ahead {{lookahead}} with suffixes of the search buffer {{search}}.
steps.match: At offset {{offset}}, the symbols match ({{expected}}). The candidate now matches {{length}} symbol(s).
steps.mismatch: At offset {{offset}}, expected {{expected}} but found {{actual}} after {{length}} match(es); stop this candidate.
steps.newBest: A longer match is best so far: {{length}} symbol(s) at offset {{offset}} ({{match}}).
steps.closerMatch: This match ties the longest length. The lecture example chooses the closer occurrence at offset {{offset}}.
steps.advance: Advance the cursor to {{cursor}}, past the match and its next symbol.
steps.decompressStart: Begin decoding {{tokens}} tag(s) into the original sequence.
steps.copyCharacter: Copy {{value}} from decoded position {{from}} into position {{to}}.
steps.appendCharacter: Append next symbol {{value}} at decoded position {{index}}.
